statements.markdown:
Let $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ be
constant with value $c$ on an open interval $I\subset(0,1)$, and let $X$
be its diffusion started at zero. Then

$$
\begin{cases}
q'''(t)\ge \dfrac1{1000c^2}
  \mathbb E\bigl[(c\Phi_{xx}(t,X_t))^4\bigr]>0,&c>0,\\[4pt]
q''(t)=\mathbb E[\Phi_{xxx}(t,X_t)^2]>0,&c=0,
\end{cases}\qquad t\in I.
$$

Thus $q'$ is strictly convex for $c>0$ and strictly increasing for
$c=0$.

statements.markdown:
**Corollary 4.2 (positive plateaus).** Suppose now that $\gamma=c>0$
on an open interval $I\subset(0,1)$ and $t\in I$. Then (4.2) gives
$q'''(t)=\mathcal C_\gamma(t)$. To establish strictness for this
limiting solution, choose $b\in I$ later than $t$ and put
$\psi=\Phi_\gamma(b,\cdot)$. This is smooth, convex, even and a
bounded distance from $|x|$, so $\psi'$ cannot be constant. The
Cole–Hopf formula gives

$$
\Phi_{xx}(t,x)
=\mathbb E^{\rm tilt}_{t,x}\psi''
  +c\operatorname{Var}^{\rm tilt}_{t,x}(\psi'),
$$
$$
\nu_{t,x}(dy)=
\frac{e^{c\psi(y)}p_{b-t}(y-x)}
 {\int_{\mathbb R}e^{c\psi(z)}p_{b-t}(z-x)\,dz}\,dy.
$$

The tilted density is positive everywhere. Its variance of the
nonconstant continuous function $\psi'$ is strictly positive; its
mean of $\psi''$ is nonnegative. Thus $v(t,x)>0$ for every $x$, and
$\mathbb E v(t,X_t)^4>0$. Combining the limiting inequality with
the differentiated identity proves
$q'''(t)\ge(1000c^2)^{-1}\mathbb E v(t,X_t)^4>0$.
This proves strict convexity of $q'$ on $I$.
statements.section: 4.5 A fixed-time inequality and its plateau application

statements.markdown:
**Lemma 2 (constant-interval curvature; [OpenAI (2026a),
Proposition 5.1][FS]).** Let $\gamma\in\mathcal U$, with its
associated diffusion and moment $q$. If $\gamma=c$ on an open
interval $I\subset(0,1)$, called a plateau, then for $t\in I$
$$
q'''(t)\geq\frac{c^2}{1000}\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^4]>0
\quad\text{if }c>0.                               \tag{3}
$$
If $c=0$, then $q''(t)=\mathbb E[\Phi_{xxx}(t,X_t)^2]>0$.

statements.markdown:
Strictness is
then established for the limit itself: the constant-coefficient heat
formula expresses $a$ as a nonnegative mean plus $c$ times a strictly
positive variance of a nonconstant slope under a positively weighted
Gaussian law. Hence $a(t,x)>0$ and its fourth moment is
positive. Positivity of the approximants alone would not suffice.
